newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon's H1 profit seen up by 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Aegon's H1 profit seen up by 22 pct.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV is likely to report first half net profits almost 22 percent higher at some 865 million guilders on Friday, analysts said on Monday.
They forecast an interim dividend of 1.40 guilders per share versus 1.18 at the half-way stage last year.
A range of forecasts put six-month net profit from ordinary operations at between 837 and 885 million guilders versus 711 million during the same period last year.
Aegon posted a net profit rise of 18.5 percent for the whole of 1996.
"The growing trend is continuing at an even stronger pace," said Tom Muller at NIB Securities.
Analysts said Aegon's life insurance activities, its core business, would continue to show good results.
"Besides this, Aegon's profits will be boosted by strong investment results (on its share portfolio)", said Jean-Paul van Bavel of Van Lanschot Bankiers.
The upward profit trend was also expected to get a lift from the stronger dollar as the U.S. currency had risen to more than 1.96 guilders at the end of June 1997 from 1.71 guilders a year earlier.

The contribution to group turnover from the U.S. will increase substantially as a result of the acquisition of the insurance activities of U.S. Providian. Prior to that deal, the U.S. market accounted for a little less than a third of turnover.

Aegon said on June 11 that it had completed the Providian insurance acquisition, saying it would add an immediate boost to group earnings and earnings per share. -- Wendy Braanker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
